business_problem: Zapier needed a better way to support AI-powered self-service analytics, conversational data access, and product personalization because legacy data silos and reliance on a central insights team meant many questions were never explored and dashboards took too long to build.
solution_summary: Zapier uses Databricks Data + AI Platform to support AI-powered self-service analytics, conversational data access, and product personalization. The implementation replaced a legacy state where legacy data silos and reliance on a central insights team meant many questions were never explored and dashboards took too long to build. Product usage data and go-to-market metrics move through production data pipelines and land in shared lakehouse datasets, giving teams one trusted data foundation. Unity Catalog governs access, lineage, and compliance across sensitive datasets. MLflow, Model Serving, and Agent Bricks operationalize models, agents, and analytics that deliver operational dashboards and conversational analytics answers.
business_outcome: Zapier improved AI-powered self-service analytics, conversational data access, and product personalization with measurable results including 2–3 hours delivering ai-powered product and business insights, 5–10x faster turnaround, and 90% of coding and querying, while giving teams a faster path from governed data to production decisions.
metrics: 2–3 hours delivering ai-powered product and business insights
Reduced dashboard creation time from 2–3 days to a few hours
Achieved up to 10x faster turnaround for analytics workflows
Shifted from 0% to ~75% of queries executed via AI-assisted workflows within 6–9 months
architecture_clues: Centralized governance, lineage, and access controls are enforced through Unity Catalog.
Operational AI workflows are deployed directly beside governed data and analytics assets.
2–3 hours delivering ai-powered product and business insights
evidence_quotes: There were so many questions teams either didn’t have the skills to answer or knew wouldn’t get prioritized by the data team, so they just never got explored.
We process data once and can decide how quickly it needs to be available,
If a use case requires data within seconds, we can make that happen without building separate systems.
With Vector Search, we now have a single pipeline to ingest and index the data, making semantic search easier and more accessible across the company,
